_doc: Sixteen tempers, one per starting character. The four axes are asked as four questions before a run; the four answers name the character the player wakes up as. See docs/13-heroes-and-tempers.md. Display text is in-world; the four-letter code is a subtitle only.

E.blurb: Counts on the room. Thinks by saying it out loud, and goes quiet when left alone too long.

I.blurb: Counts on themselves. Arrives at the fire with the thinking already done.

S.blurb: Trusts the track, the weather and the wound. Goes and looks.

N.blurb: Trusts the shape of the thing. Knows where it is going before it gets there.

T.blurb: Decides by weight. Counts the cost first and the company second.

F.blurb: Decides by who it lands on. Counts the company first and the cost after.

J.blurb: Decides early and holds. Walks in knowing where they sleep.

P.blurb: Decides late and keeps moving. Lets the country say what it wants.

quiz.prompt: The company makes camp after a bad day on the road. The fire is lit and nobody has said much.

options.text: Start talking. Whatever is wrong only gets worse in the quiet.
Take the first watch. You think better with the fire at your back.

quiz.prompt: A village swears the bridge is out. You can see the river from where you stand, an hour off.

options.text: Walk down and look at the bridge.
Ask who told them, and when. A rumour that old has already changed shape.

quiz.prompt: Someone you hired three weeks ago is slowing the company down, and knows it.

options.text: Pay them out and part at the next town. The road does not care who tried.
Keep them on. They came when it was asked, and that is worth carrying.

quiz.prompt: Dawn, and a gate two days east. You are carrying four days of food.

options.text: Fix the route tonight — where you sleep, and where you turn back.
Start walking. The country will tell you what it wants on the way.

leans._doc: One nudge per letter. Every character carries exactly four, one per axis, so nobody is strictly stronger — sixteen mixes of one budget.

INTJ.blurb: Has already decided how this ends and is walking the rest of you toward it.

INTP.blurb: Would rather understand the gate than close it, and says so at the worst moment.

ENTJ.blurb: Takes the road in hand within a day of joining it. Nobody votes.

ENTP.blurb: Finds the hole in every plan, including the ones that were working.

INFJ.blurb: Carries one conviction a long way without mentioning it until it costs something.

INFP.blurb: Yields on everything except the one thing, and never on that.

ENFJ.blurb: Arrives alone and leaves with four people who would follow them anywhere.

ENFP.blurb: Talks a closed town open, then wants to know what is behind the next hill.

ISTJ.blurb: Knows what is in the packs, what it cost, and who was owed.

ISFJ.blurb: Notices who has not eaten. Remembers the names of the dead longer than anyone.

ESTJ.blurb: Says the hard thing first, in front of everyone, and means it kindly.

ESFJ.blurb: Makes a camp into a household by the second night, whether or not it was wanted.

ISTP.blurb: Says little, fixes what is broken, and is already moving when it goes wrong.

ISFP.blurb: Goes where they were going. Will not be argued out of it and will not argue back.

ESTP.blurb: Is across the room before the rest of you have agreed there is a problem.

ESFP.blurb: Makes the worst week on the road into something the company tells stories about.
